product_category.value: Immersive VR simulation platform dedicated exclusively to nursing education and training, designed by nurses for nurses

evidence.quote: UbiSim is dedicated exclusively to nursing education simulation and Virtual Reality.
UbiSim is a leading virtual reality training provider for nursing programs.
The UbiSim immersive virtual reality simulation platform is built by nurses, for nurses to meet the evolving needs of nurse learners in higher education and healthcare institutions.

product_category.note: Nursing only; no other disciplines are named. The first quote is the homepage META DESCRIPTION line. The about-us page adds 'UbiSim is a Labster product.'

evidence.quote: UbiSim provides complete visual and haptic immersion, compatible with commercially available Meta headsets and controllers.
UbiSim works on the entire wireless Quest family of headsets, including Meta Quest 2, Meta Quest 3 and Meta Quest Pro.
UbiSim runs on standalone VR headsets, and headsets are typically procured separately from your software license.

platforms.note: Learners use Meta Quest standalone headsets (Quest 2, Quest 3, Quest Pro named); headsets are not included with a purchase. The computer side is described as a facilitator tool: 'A laptop or desktop computer with Windows/Mac operating system and Chrome browser. No software installation required.' and 'A facilitator to operate the computer' (how-it-works), so Web is not listed. Learners do touch the computer in two places, which could argue for Web or Desktop on review: in peer-to-peer mode one learner is 'triggering the preset dialogs on the computer', and 'Peers can learn by actively observing the simulation on their computers' (how-it-works). The pricing page also lists 'web replay' as part of debriefing. None of these says the learner simulation itself runs in a browser.

key_capabilities.note: AI status conflicts across pages: the AI page says 'Coming soon: AI-Supported Dialogue and other AI enhancements' and its META DESCRIPTION says 'Coming November 2025', with a roadmap disclaimer that features 'may be modified, delayed, or abandoned'; the pricing page lists 'AI-powered patient dialogue' and 'Instant, AI-enhanced performance reports' under 'What’s Included' with no 'coming soon' label. Dialogue is also described differently: how-it-works mentions 'preset dialogs' triggered on the computer, while the healthcare page says 'unscripted dialogue'. Other features stated but not listed: unfolding medical orders that appear as a scenario progresses; editable patient characteristics (age, race, gender identity, language), medications, equipment, room layout; 'Multi-tiered debriefing with self-guided reflection, quizzes, and web replay'; casting the facilitator screen or headset view to a large screen; catalog filters by system, learner level and type of care; implementation packages (Basic, Essentials, Custom); 'Hardware distribution and management assistance'. The healthcare page claims 'UbiSim is the only VR nursing platform with an intuitive editor.'

evidence.quote: UbiSim’s pricing depends on a few factors specific to your program:
Yes. Annual engagements typically begin at $5,000 USD, depending on the solution and implementation requirements.
Implementation is a separate one-time package. UbiSim offers three tiers: Basic (~5 weeks), Essentials (~6 weeks), and Custom (scoped pricing and timing).
Yes, UbiSim offers free trials for qualified buyers.

pricing.note: The factors listed after the first quote are 'Learner volume discounts', 'Term length options' and 'Implementation tiers'; the page has 'Get a Quote' buttons. No per-seat or per-learner price and no prices for the implementation tiers are published. Learners do not pay directly (institution or program license). The intuitive-editor page says the editor is 'Included at no extra charge'.
